notes: Summary: Evaluating Redwood Dedicated for low-latency chat + reranking at scale. Primary ask: predictable throughput (150-200 rps), p95 latency SLOs, and a deterministic cost model for reserved GPUs.
POC ask: 8-GPU runway preferred but starting pilot at 4 GPUs. Want clear breakpoint analysis for moving to 8 vs 16 GPUs.

Commit level options (vendor proposal draft): 4 GPU reserved (pilot), 8 GPU reserved (recommended mid-tier), 16 GPU reserved (scale). Vendor list price used for modeling: $4,500/GPU/month (placeholder for negotiations).

Utilization assumptions: engineering recommended steady-state util = 60% (avg request mix), peak bursts to 85% for 2-3 hours/day. Cache & batching expected to reduce effective compute by ~30% on reranking-heavy workloads.

Unit economics rough calc (for model family X, quantized 4-bit): tokens/sec per GPU conservative = 30 tps. tokens/month/GPU = 30 * 3600 * 24 * 30 = ~77.76M tokens. Cost/GPU/month = $4,500 => raw cost per token ≈ $4,500 / 77.76M ≈ $5.8e-5 per token => ~$0.058 per 1k tokens.
Adjusted cost with caching/ batching (30% reduction) => effective per 1k tokens ≈ $0.041. If utilization falls to 40%, unit cost rises to ~$0.087 per 1k tokens (no caching).

Hosted break-even: Redwood hosted API ~ $0.06 per 1k tokens (team supplied comparator). Dedicated break-even at given pricing occurs at ~35-40% utilization for this model family. Above that, reserved capacity is cheaper and predictable.

Recommendation: Start POC with 8-GPU reserved commitment for 3 months with monthly review. 8 GPUs gives headroom for autoscale/burst and makes price/arr math match their ARR target. Insert automatic fallback to hosted for >95th percentile traffic to avoid over-commit.

SLA negotiation points to push in legal: include latency SLOs per model family (p50/p95/p99), credits for missed performance, transparent kernel/quantization changes, and obligation to provide model-variant fallbacks if a GPU family is deprecated.
Operational asks from customer: dedicated metrics per-route (token breakdown), token-level billing, per-model latency histograms, and long-term log retention for audit (90-180 days).

Risk notes: if customer standardizes on 70B dense models with higher memory/latency profile, effective tokens/sec drops 40%, which increases per-token cost materially — negotiation should include a glide-path discount for model-family migration or a guaranteed uplift in commit credits.
Quote from CTO on 2026-02-18 call: "We need economics that don't surprise us at scale — predictable $/1k tokens and hard SLOs for p95."

Next technical step: run 72-hour throughput stress on 8-GPU config with production cache layers enabled and collect per-model p50/p95/p99, KV cache hit rates, and batching efficiency. Legal to push draft SLA with latency credits and KMS attestation before April close.
